key_insight: SVR teaches a model to self-verifiy its own answers and decide when to stop, turning test-time compute into a learned adaptive policy instead of a fixed budget.
engineering_relevance: This is useful for reasoning systems that need better accuracy-per-compute by spending extra turns only on hard problems while keeping easy ones cheap.
method: Multi-turn RL with GRPO trains the model to output a solution, a discrete correctness verdict, and a confidence score at each turn.
The model keeps an answer only when the verdict is Correct and confidence is above a threshold; otherwise it continues refining with its own self-verification.
Ground-truth labels are used only for training rewards, not as verifier feedback during refinement or inference.
evidence_signal: On seven math reasoning benchmarks with Qwen3.5-2B, SVR reached 0.563 macro-average accuracy using only 2.99 turns on average.
watch_item: Performance depends on learned calibration of verdict and confidence, so miscalibration or threshold sensitivity could reduce the benefit of adaptive stopping.
paper_title: SVR: Self-Verifying Refinement via Joint Verdict-Confidence Reinforcement Learning for Adaptive Test-Time Compute
